title: Who is a preceptor, and what direct supervision of a pharmacy intern involves
subtopic: Preceptor qualifications and direct supervision of interns
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 2.00 a Preceptor is a registered pharmacist in good standing who has completed at least one year of the actual practice of pharmacy and whom the Board has approved to supervise and direct the training of pharmacy interns and to assist in the training of other pharmacy interns. Direct Supervision, as it applies to a pharmacy intern, is the type of supervision a Board-approved registered pharmacist preceptor in a pharmacy, pharmacy department, or institutional pharmacy is required to provide to a pharmacy intern when the preceptor oversees and directs the professional activities of the pharmacy intern, and it includes directly reviewing the work of the intern. The definition of Pharmacy Intern describes an individual registered by the Board to acquire, under the direction of a Board-approved registered pharmacist preceptor to whom he or she has been assigned, the practical experience that is a prerequisite to examination for personal registration as a pharmacist, and provides that a pharmacy intern may engage in the full range of activities conducted by a registered pharmacist provided that at all times he or she is under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor.
exam_relevance: Tests who qualifies to supervise a Massachusetts pharmacy intern (a registered pharmacist in good standing, with at least one year of actual practice, approved by the Board) and that direct supervision of an intern means overseeing and directing the intern's professional activities, including directly reviewing the intern's work.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations
authority.section: 247 CMR 2.00, definitions of Direct Supervision (a), Pharmacy Intern and Preceptor

numeric_facts.fact: actual practice of pharmacy a registered pharmacist must have completed to be a preceptor
numeric_facts.conditions: the pharmacist must also be registered, in good standing and approved by the Board to supervise and direct the training of pharmacy interns

common_confusions: A pharmacist with less than one year of actual practice, not in good standing, or not approved by the Board is not a preceptor.
Direct supervision of an intern includes directly reviewing the intern's work; it is not satisfied by presence alone.
verification_notes: Read in the official Board of Registration in Pharmacy publication of 247 CMR 2.00 (the mass.gov PDF) on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
